title: Knower of every heart
hookLine: ghat ghat ke antar kee jaanat: He knows every heart and recognizes the pain of good and bad alike (Chaupai)

lines: PARTLY HIDDEN, EVEN FROM LOVED ONES.
cards: There's a particular loneliness in being misunderstood. You did something for a good reason, and someone took it the worst way. Or you're carrying a pain nobody can see, so people treat you as if you're fine.

Or, harder, you did something wrong, you know it, and nobody can see the mess of reasons and hurt underneath. Plenty of people walk around partly hidden, even from those who love them, sometimes especially from them.
Chaupai has a line for that hiddenness, and it goes further than you'd expect.

teach.b: The line is ghat ghat ke antar kee jaanat, bhale bure kee peer pachhaanat. Ghat ghat: every vessel, every body, every heart. Ke antar kee jaanat: knows what's inside.
Bhale bure: the good and the bad. Kee peer pachhaanat: recognizes the pain of. He knows what's within every heart, and recognizes the pain of the good and the bad alike.
The first half is something Sikh scripture says often: God is antarjami, the inner knower, who sees from inside. The second half is the surprise.

teach.h: THE PAIN OF THE BAD, TOO.
teach.b: The pain of the bad. Not just the good person's suffering; the wrongdoer's too. The person who hurt you has a pain underneath it, and in this line, God recognizes that as well.
It doesn't excuse anything; the same prayer has just asked for wrongdoers to be stopped. But it refuses to pretend that anyone, good or bad, is only their actions.
Peer, the word for pain here, is close to an ordinary Punjabi word for an ache, the kind you'd mention to a doctor. That's how close this knowing is.
And the other side: if the One knows every heart, you are known, completely. Your good reasons nobody saw. Your hidden ache.
Even the tangle behind what you're ashamed of. For some people that sounds frightening.
Chaupai sets it inside a prayer for protection, so it's meant to sound like rest.
In the prayer's picture, the one praying has nothing to explain. They're already understood.

how: Many Sikhs recite this line within Chaupai Sahib morning and evening, and Sikh scripture often names God as antarjami, the inner knower of every heart.

o: a judge who weighs every deed
a saint who reads people's minds
the inner knower of every heart

games.q: knower of every heart — tap the pairs.

s: the line says God recognizes only the pain of good people
bhale bure kee peer pachhaanat: the pain of the good and the bad alike.
antarjami, the inner knower, is a name for God in Sikh scripture
the One who sees every heart from inside.
recognizing a wrongdoer's pain means excusing what they did
the same prayer asks for wrongdoers to be stopped. it just won't reduce anyone to their actions.

games.q: someone has hurt you badly. Chaupai says the One knows every heart. whose pain does the line say God recognizes?
o: the pain of the good and the bad alike.
games.why: bhale bure kee peer pachhaanat: the pain of the good and the bad. it doesn't excuse the harm, but it sees what's underneath.

practice: Bring to mind something about yourself that nobody fully understands, an old hurt, a reason never said out loud, a quiet worry, and let it be there without fixing or explaining it.
Picture it already seen, completely, by someone who isn't shocked. If you pray, say Waheguru and let the One who knows every heart hold it; if not, just practice not hiding it from yourself.

wordCard.voice: Antarjami, the inner knower. Ghat ghat ke antar kee jaanat: the One knows what's inside every heart, and recognizes the pain of the good and the bad alike.
